reviews.title: Completely Unreliable. Ethically Questionable. An Absolute Disgrace.
reviews.text:
I have used Alarm Clock Pro for over ten years. I paid for the full version because I believed in supporting developers who build reliable tools. I trusted this app to do one simple, critical job: wake me up.

Today it failed.

Overnight, my iPhone updated. By morning, your app was a corpse. It won’t open — just an inert logo sitting on the screen like a monument to negligence. No error message. No explanation. No warning. Just silence.

Because of that silence, I overslept for work.

An alarm clock that stops working without notice is not a minor inconvenience — it’s a liability. People depend on these apps for jobs, travel, medical appointments, responsibilities. You don’t get to treat that casually.

And then comes the real insult.

I attempt to reinstall the app I already paid for, only to be greeted with a £19.99-per-year subscription demand. Annual. For something I purchased outright years ago. The “Restore Purchases” button does nothing. Absolutely nothing.

So let’s call this what it looks like:
Long-time customers abandoned. Paid upgrades erased. A silent forced migration to subscription. No transparency. No courtesy. No integrity.

If you were discontinuing support for legacy versions, you had a responsibility to communicate that clearly and prominently. You didn’t.

Instead, you left loyal users to discover it by oversleeping for work.

Ten years of support repaid with a broken app and a paywall ultimatum.

An alarm clock has one job: reliability. When that fails,

reviews.title: Ads preventing app from doing its job
reviews.text: I really love this app, and for the longest time it would really save me in the mornings. The sound options are super nice as well as the Brightnes options, and overall it's a great app. However, I've run into an issue with ads. I understand the app is free and in order to benefit, it needs ads and I never have an issue with banner ads or anything, but recent ads that pop up and cover the screen to play a video ad affect the apps ability to work as intended. If an ad pops up on screen and I'm unable to ex out of it (because I'm asleep) the alarm will not sound, and its happened almost every night. I'll wake up hours past my alarm, none of my house mates heard it going off (which they usually do but it wakes me fast enough to turn it off when it works that they don't mind) and there's an ad on screen. I really love this app and I don't want to switch to another because no other alarm apps have been effective the way this one is, but if it's preventing itself from doing the one thing it's meant to, I won't be able to continue using it.

reviews.title: Unreliable
reviews.text: I have been using this app for several years, and I really love the features. However, three times in the last month or two, it failed to play the alarm sound. The first two, I thought maybe I just slept through it, or I did something wrong, but the third time, I actually woke up just before the alarm and was looking at the screen when the time for the alarm arrived, and absolutely nothing happened. It displayed the time but made no sound. It didn’t even show the buttons to stop or snooze. I am a software developer and understand that bugs sometimes happen. But this bug is so fundamentally serious that I cannot trust this company. I love this app, but if it is not reliable, I cannot continue to use it. I have canceled my subscription and deleted the app.

This is extremely sneaky and underhand as I bought a product outright and was never told it was only for a certain number of years.  This is made worse by the fact that the subscription version is virtually identical to what I originally bought.  I might be more sympathetic if the new version is substantially changed or if the cost of subscribing was more reasonable.  To pay £10 a month (with no explanation of the differences between the various subscription prices) to use very simple software is crazy.  Your greed and lack of morality has driven a loyal customer away.  Shame on you.
